papers.title: Forest pest prediction using a hybrid Random Forest–LSTM model
papers.authors: Jiaqi Xu, Jiaqi Zhang, Xiumei Mo, Guofei Fang, Chengdong Xu
papers.abstract: Introduction Forest pest outbreaks can substantially affect forest ecosystem stability and pose challenges to forest health monitoring and risk management. However, forest pest monitoring datasets commonly contain a high proportion of zero observations and exhibit pronounced temporal variability, which can limit the predictive performance of conventional machine learning approaches. To address these challenges, this study developed a hybrid RF-LSTM framework incorporating Zero-Inflated Poisson (ZIP) features and LSTM-derived temporal features to evaluate the effects of these feature enhancements on Random Forest (RF) model performance. Methods Multi-station daily monitoring data for Coleoptera and Lepidoptera in Rui’an City, Zhejiang Province, China, were used to evaluate the proposed framework. The ZIP model was first employed to characterize the zero inflation structure of pest occurrence data, while the LSTM network was used to extract temporal representations from sequences of meteorological, seasonal, and ZIP-derived features. papers.title: Climatic Suitability and Invasion Risk of the Elm Zigzag Sawfly in North America
papers.authors: Claudia Nuñez‐Penichet, Zenia Ruiz-Utrilla, Daniel Rojas-Ariza, Weverton Carlos Ferreira Trindade, Joanna L. Corimanya
papers.abstract: The elm zigzag sawfly, Aproceros leucopoda (Hymenoptera), native to eastern Asia, is among the most concerning potential pests for elm trees (Ulmus spp.); elms form an important component in many North Temperate forests. This sawfly species invaded Europe in 2003 and spread rapidly across much of that continent. In 2020, it was recorded in North America, and it has since become established in several parts of the eastern United States and Canada. Sawfly infestations can cause severe elm tree defoliation, branch die-back that weakens tree health, and potentially tree mortality. Sawfly invasions have the potential to further exacerbate elm decline, especially in conjunction with other pressures, including Dutch elm disease (Ophiostoma ulmi). We used rigorous approaches from distributional ecology to explore climatic suitability for A. leucopoda across North America, considering various sources of uncertainty in the data. We found that, without control, the elm zigzag sawfly could establish populations across eastern Canada and much of the central-eastern and northeastern United States, as well as in the Pacific Northwest. papers.title: Evaluating MaxEnt Modeling Strategies for Mapping the Climatic Suitability of Five Pest Insects in the Contiguous United States Under Climate Change Scenarios
papers.authors: Pankaj Chouhan, Olmo Zavala‐Romero, Muhammad A. Haseeb
papers.abstract: Species distribution models depend on modeling choices. We used MaxEnt for five pest insects in the contiguous United States, four introduced and one native: the brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys), corn earworm (Helicoverpa zea, native), spongy moth (Lymantria dispar dispar), Diaprepes root weevil (Diaprepes abbreviatus) and spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula). Models trained on US records and the 1970–2000 climate were projected to 2021–2040 and 2041–2060 under four emission pathways with five climate models, mainly ACCESS-CM2. We varied m, the share of background points drawn near the records over the whole country and inside species-specific accessible areas. No single m was best in either extent. The Boyce index separated the settings, while the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) changed little for m≤0.75. Removing out-of-range records made a uniform background clearly best for the spongy moth. Averaged over climate models, the suitable area decreased by 2041–2060 for four species and increased for the root weevil. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. papers.title: Quantifying Domain Shift in Peach Leaf Damage Classification: An Evaluation of Attention Mechanisms and Fine-Tuning Strategies
papers.authors: Adrián Cánovas-Rodríguez, Miguel A. González-Illán, Maria Fernanda García-Cruz, P. Tortosa, J.S. Rubio-Asensio
papers.abstract: Leaf damage classifiers are usually trained and evaluated on public images collected elsewhere, and their behaviour in a new orchard is rarely measured. We quantified this gap for peach leaves. Eleven ImageNet-pretrained convolutional backbones, each with and without a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), were trained on 1415 public leaves (six classes). They were evaluated, with photograph-grouped cross-validation and confidence intervals, on 182 leaves from 122 photographs taken in a commercial orchard (four classes). On the public hold-out set, macro-F1 ranged from 0.670 to 0.772, and the ranking of the best models was not resolved; CBAM brought no improvement (pooled change −0.009 to −0.001). Without retraining, mean orchard macro-F1 was 0.634, against 0.719 on the same four public classes, but only after masking the two classes absent from the orchard; without masking, one-third of the leaves were assigned to them. Label-free normalisation-statistics alignment did not help, whereas fine-tuning raised the mean macro-F1 to 0.72, and a few tens of labelled leaves sufficed to match zero-shot transfer. papers.title: Plant bioluminescence for sustainable horticulture: Living biosensors, crop sentinels and precision crop monitoring
papers.authors: Parbin Huda Baruah
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Ecology and Conservation
papers.abstract: Bioluminescence, although frequently framed as an ecological curiosity of fireflies, marine macrofauna and glow-in-the-dark fungi, has become a real-world tool for understanding plant biology. Over many decades, firefly luciferase-based reporter systems have facilitated sensitive and quantitative measurements of gene expression, circadian rhythms and signalling in living plants. The ability to achieve bioluminescence within a single organism, where both luciferase and its substrate are produced on demand, has only recently been realised through the construction of bacterial, for example *Vibrio*, and fungal light-producing pathways. This transition is particularly relevant to agriculture and horticulture, where repeated, non-destructive monitoring can be achieved without external luciferin application. This article connects the molecular basis of different bioluminescence systems with their recent applications in crop and horticultural research. Particular focus is placed on autonomous reporters for defence hormones, pattern-triggered immunity and viral infection, sentinel plants for protected cultivation, high-throughput phenotyping and breeding, and lux-based microbial biosensors

papers.authors: Yuanxiang Shi, Xinwei Liu, Xiyu Zhang, Baoguo Shi, Xiaohe Wang
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Health Geographics
papers.abstract: Low levels of physical activity (LPA) remain an important and unevenly distributed global public health problem, contributing substantially to the burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs). However, the burden attributable to LPA varies considerably across geographic regions and population groups and has changed over time. This study aimed to characterize the temporal trends, population differences, spatial clustering, and geographic variation in the burden of NCDs attributable to LPA at the global, regional, and national levels. We analyzed GBD 2021 data for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and age-period-cohort (APC) analysis was conducted across SDI groups. Global Moran’s I and Getis-Ord Gi* were applied to examine spatial autocorrelation and identify hot and cold spots in ASDR. Associations with socioeconomic, environmental, and behavioral factors were further examined by comparing OLS, TWR, GWR, and GTWR models, with GWR selected for the spatial analysis of local coefficients. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. papers.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females.
